title: GitHub Actions Introduction
subtitle: .github/workflows/, YAML structure, jobs, steps, runners — the anatomy of a workflow

content.text: GitHub Actions is GitHub's built-in CI/CD platform — free for public repos, generous free tier for private ones. Workflows are defined in YAML files inside .github/workflows/. When events happen (push, PR, schedule), GitHub spins up a fresh virtual machine (a runner), clones your repo, and runs your workflow. No server to configure, no plugins to install.

content.code:
# Every workflow has a name (shown in GitHub UI)
name: CI

# ── on: TRIGGER ──────────────────────────────────────────
# When should this workflow run?
on:
  push:
    branches: [main, dev]          # on push to these branches
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]               # on PR targeting main
  workflow_dispatch:               # manual trigger from GitHub UI

# ── jobs ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Jobs run in PARALLEL by default (unless needs: is specified)
jobs:

  # Job 1: run tests
  test:
    # The OS to run on — ubuntu-latest is the most common
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    # ── steps: the actual commands ──────────────────────
    steps:
      # Every workflow starts by checking out your code
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      # Set up Node.js
      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '20'
          cache: 'npm'              # cache node_modules between runs

      # Install dependencies
      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      # Run tests
      - name: Run tests
        run: npm test

  # Job 2: lint (runs in parallel with test)
  lint:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with: { node-version: '20', cache: 'npm' }
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm run lint

  # Job 3: only runs if test AND lint pass
  build:
    needs: [test, lint]             # wait for both jobs to succeed
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with: { node-version: '20', cache: 'npm' }
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm run build

items: Workflow — the YAML file. One repo can have multiple workflows (ci.yml, deploy.yml, release.yml).
Job — a group of steps that run on one runner. Jobs run in parallel by default.
Step — a single task: either a shell command (run:) or a pre-built action (uses:).
Action — a reusable step from the GitHub Marketplace. actions/checkout@v4 clones your repo. actions/setup-node@v4 installs Node.js.
Runner — the VM that executes the job. ubuntu-latest, windows-latest, macos-latest are GitHub-hosted. You can also self-host.
Context — runtime data available via ${{ }}: ${{ github.sha }}, ${{ github.actor }}, ${{ secrets.MY_SECRET }}.

content.code:
steps:
  - name: Print useful context values
    run: |
      echo "Branch: ${{ github.ref_name }}"
      echo "Commit SHA: ${{ github.sha }}"
      echo "Actor (who triggered): ${{ github.actor }}"
      echo "Event: ${{ github.event_name }}"
      echo "Repo: ${{ github.repository }}"

  # Conditional step — only on main branch
  - name: Deploy (only on main)
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    run: ./deploy.sh

  # Environment-specific step
  - name: Set image tag
    run: echo "IMAGE_TAG=${{ github.sha }}" >> $GITHUB_ENV

  - name: Use the tag set above
    run: echo "Building image:$IMAGE_TAG"

content.text: Always pin action versions. Use actions/checkout@v4 not actions/checkout@latest. Pinning to a major version (v4) protects you from breaking changes while still getting patches. For maximum security, pin to a full SHA: actions/checkout@9bb56186c3edbf8a20b5...@v4

questions.question: In a workflow with jobs 'test', 'lint', and 'build' (with needs: [test, lint]), how do the jobs execute?
options: All three run sequentially: test → lint → build
test and lint run in parallel; build only starts after both succeed
test and lint run in parallel; build runs immediately in parallel too
Only the first job runs, then the others are skipped
questions.explanation: Jobs without 'needs:' run in parallel. 'build' has needs: [test, lint], so it waits for both to complete successfully. If either test or lint fails, build is skipped. This lets you run independent checks in parallel (faster) while still ensuring build only runs after validation passes.

faq.q: How much does GitHub Actions cost?
faq.a: Public repositories: completely free, unlimited minutes. Private repositories: 2,000 minutes/month free on GitHub Free, 3,000 on Pro, 50,000 on Teams. ubuntu-latest uses 1 minute of quota per minute of compute. macOS uses 10× (10 minutes quota per minute). Most projects stay within the free tier.
